notes: No context at all. Two motivating scenarios collapse into this same input because the agent has no telemetry to tell them apart: (1) beam dump (accelerator-level beam loss, no ring-current/beam-status signal reaches the agent) — wants confirm-beam-status + pause; (2) sample holder frame entering the field of view (x-ray-opaque frame material causes an expected, benign intensity drop) — wants no action, just a visual confirm. SampleX/SampleY moves that would hint at (2) are deliberately excluded from the event stream (controller.py _INTEL_MOTORS, they move every line during a scan) so the agent cannot distinguish these cases today. Correct behavior for this tuple: hedge — name both a serious hypothesis (beam dump) and a benign one (sample holder/frame), recommend confirming rather than committing to either. See handles_ambiguous_total_loss in run_assertions.py for the split-tuple TODO once beam-status telemetry exists.

Energy changed — shifts focal length in zone-plate systems (f proportional to 1/E). Genuinely relevant (Energy is the actual cause), but challenging: the coupling is non-obvious and a naive diagnosis might miss it.
Both ZonePlateZ and SampleZ moved — ambiguous which caused it

Large Energy jump recently (e.g. crossing an undulator harmonic boundary) without repositioning dependent optics (mirrors, aperture, grating) — a common novice-user mistake. beamline_database.py stores an energy->optics lookup table (harmonic, grating, exit slit, m121/m101 mirror angles, EPU offset) but AgentInterface has no code-level access to it and no domain hints in its system prompt; it must reason about the coupling from general knowledge. Correct behavior: recognize the recent large energy change as the likely cause and recommend re-checking/re-aligning dependent optics.

Same large Energy jump as id=21, plus an unrelated ZonePlateZ move also in the event log as a distractor. Correct behavior: attribute the drop to the energy change/optics misalignment, not the ZonePlateZ move (which affects focus, not intensity).

SampleZ moved much further than a routine focus tweak (optics chain is beam -> central stopper -> zone plate -> OSA -> sample, so moving the sample too far upstream risks physically contacting/displacing the OSA). Placeholder magnitude — not a calibrated real travel limit, update if a real safe-range spec becomes available. Real hardware-damage risk (task_agent/tools.py explicitly forbids moving OSA_Z directly), so this should be treated with urgency, not just a data-quality note. Correct behavior: recommend moving the sample away from the optics and running an OSA (focus) scan to confirm the OSA position/ZonePlateZ-offset calibration is still good.

Diode (Detector Y motor) was parked out of frame earlier in the session (e.g. for a ptychography/CCD acquisition), then a diode-based scan (e.g. STXM) started without moving it back — so the diode reads low/no signal. Correct behavior: recognize the diode isn't in its home/in-frame position and recommend moving the detector back to (0,0). Note: (0,0) is correct for this eval's target beamline (ALS 7.0.1.2 / COSMIC, per memory/project_goals.md) — the same pystxmcontrol software runs at other beamlines where blindly moving to (0,0) could be unsafe, so this fix is beamline-specific, not a general rule.

Same Energy move as id=15. Real cause candidate #1: the per-scan 'autofocus' checkbox (mainwindow.ui autofocusCheckbox, scan['autofocus']) was unchecked, so the scan never re-issued the ZonePlateZ move to the calibrated focus position when energy changed (base_scan.py handle_energy_and_focus: ZP move only happens 'if self.scan.get("autofocus", False)'). KNOWN TELEMETRY GAP, tested anyway as an honest baseline: IntelligenceModule.on_scan_start() (intelligence.py) does not forward scan['autofocus'] into the scan_start event, so recent_events carries no signal either way — this tuple and id=26 have identical inputs to id=15 by necessity. Expected to fail often today; the point is to quantify the gap, not to hide it. Fix (deliberately not applied as part of this eval work): add autofocus=scan.get('autofocus') to the recorder.record(...) call in on_scan_start().

Same Energy move as id=15 and id=25. Real cause candidate #2: autofocus was on and the ZonePlateZ move to the calibrated position did happen, but landed in the wrong place because the A0/A1 zone-plate-position-vs-energy equation (calibratedPosition = A0 - A1*energy, derivedEnergy.py; config/motor.json Energy: A0=0, A1=13.2444) is stale/miscalibrated. Same known telemetry gap as id=25 — recent_events has no way to signal calibration drift, so this is also tested as an honest current-state baseline, not a case we expect to reliably pass yet.
